question: The O-ring's compression reaction over the squeeze window — the datum 52 replaced with a generous bound, 73 judged the collar wall against, and 87's (A) needs from below.

source.read: 2026-10-13, vector coordinates of the PDF page (pdftocairo -svg)
source.temperature: §3.8: force decreases very little with temperature except the hardest compounds (N0674-70: −10 % from 24 to 126 °C)
source.time: §2.4.11: compression set is the same relaxation (100 % = no force), reported only after 70 h at 100 °C — no field-life figure

assumptions: log-load linear in squeeze between the chart's rows
seal length = mean circumference on the groove's inner wall (ring stretched onto it)
the unconfined bars hold at an 80 % gland fill

end_of_service.is: a requirement on the compound's stress relaxation over 20 years, not a force this source gives

missing_data: the compound's own compression-load curve at 19–30 % for CS 1.78 (Parker's bar spans compounds)
its stress relaxation over the service life at the capsule's envelope (ISO 3384-type data)
the cold-side stiffening of EPDM (raises the reaction; adverse for the lug, favourable for (A))
verdict: The «generous» 100 N is not an upper bound: Parker's 70 Shore A bar for the .070 section puts the ring's reaction at 64–218 N at the 24.5 % nominal and up to 409 N at the 30 % window top, and the band's high end passes 100 N already at 17.1 % squeeze. With that high end, 52's requirement (lift / 0.65) asks 338 N at the nominal — the lug root still carries it at the print floor (1.35×, SF 2 inside) — but 632 N at the window top (0.72×): above 27.1 % squeeze a compound at the hard end of the bar makes strength, not printability, size the collar wall — 0.28 mm at the window top against the 0.2 mm print floor; the chain 52 models today ends at 27.3 % (0.98×). From below, the ring starts at no less than 40 N at the 19 % floor, so 87's (A) holds at the end of service only if the ring keeps 26 % of its initial reaction after 20 years — a compound datum Parker does not give.
